chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) supplicated for rain and the people were given to drink until they said, 'It is drowning (flood)!' and the Messenger of Allah gestured with his hand and turned it back, saying: 'O Allah, around us and not upon us!' He said: So the clouds dispersed.

And they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you supplicated for rain for us but we were not given to drink, then you supplicated for rain for us and we were given to drink.' He said: 'Indeed I supplicated and there was no intention for me in that; then I supplicated and I had an intention in that.'

key_terms.اسْتَسْقَى: supplicated for rain (istisqa); the formal rain prayer performed in times of drought
key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ حَوَالَيْنَا وَلَا عَلَيْنَا: O Allah, around us and not upon us; the Prophet's prayer to redirect flood-level rain to the surrounding lands
key_terms.نِيَّةٌ: intention (niyya); the inner resolve and purpose behind a religious act, held to be essential for its acceptance

ai.seo_question: Why was the Prophet's first rain supplication not answered while his second was? What does this hadith teach about the importance of intention (niyya) in supplication?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) through a chain of trusted Kufan transmitters, recounts an episode from the life of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in which he performed two rain supplications (istisqa). The first supplication was fulfilled with abundant rain that threatened to flood; the Prophet then gestured and prayed 'O Allah, around us and not upon us,' and the clouds dispersed. When asked by the Companions why the first supplication went unanswered while the second was granted, the Prophet explained that the crucial difference was the presence or absence of sincere intention (niyya). This account was preserved in the chapter on 'devotion upon supplication' in al-Kafi to emphasize the essential role of inner sincerity in du'a — a central theme where the spirit behind an act is as important as its external form.
word_analysis: and we were given to drink

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> supplicated for the rain and the people were drenched to the extent that they said, ‘It’s drowning (us)’, and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said (gestured) by his<sup>saww</sup> hand and returned it: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Around us and not upon us!” 
He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘So the clouds dispersed,

and they said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>! You<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> supplicated for the rain for us but we were not quenched, then you<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> supplicated for the rain for us, so we were quenched’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> supplicated and there was no intention for me<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> during that, then I<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> supplicated, and for me<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> there was an intention regarding that’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

When the Messenger of Allah prayed for rain, people were drenched so much that they thought they might be drowned and the Messenger of Allah made hand gestures to scatter the cloud, saying, ‘O Lord make it to rain around us, not on us.’ The Imam said, ‘The clouds scattered

and people asked, “O Messenger of Allah, how is it that once you prayed for rain it did not rain, then you prayed for rain and it rained?” The Messenger of Allah said, ‘I prayed but 1 did not have much intention, then I prayed and I did.’”
